claims.reason: `[T2Space G]` is an argument of the theorem: it is instance-implicit and only mentions `G`, which the statement uses. Nothing in the statement needs it. `C(G ⧸ H, G)`, the quotient and `QuotientGroup.mk` need only the group and topology structures. In the proof it is used only as an instance argument of `quotientMapOfLE_exists_continuous_section_of_isClosed` (ContinuousSection.lean:395). It can be derived from the other hypotheses. Mathlib's `TotallyDisconnectedSpace.t1Space` (Topology/Separation/Connected.lean:22) is an instance that needs only `[TopologicalSpace X] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace X]`, so `isClosed_singleton : IsClosed ({1} : Set G)` holds. `IsTopologicalGroup.t2Space_iff_one_closed` (Topology/Algebra/Group/Pointwise.lean:407) needs only `[TopologicalSpace G] [Group G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]`, with `G` implicit, and its `.2` direction turns `IsClosed {1}` into `T2Space G`. So `omit [T2Space G] in` on the theorem, plus `haveI : T2Space G := IsTopologicalGroup.t2Space_iff_one_closed.2 isClosed_singleton` at the start of the proof, gives the instance, and the rest of the proof is unchanged. The argument works for every group, including the trivial one, so there is no degenerate case.
